title: WATER GOVERNANCE AND CONTROL: EVIDENCE FROM STATE WATER UTILITIES IN NORTHERN MALAYSIA

WATER GOVERNANCE AND CONTROL: EVIDENCE FROM STATE WATER UTILITIES IN NORTHERN MALAYSIA

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Nurizyan Samsudin, Sakinah Muslim, Vally Senasi

ABSTRACT

Water utilities in Northern Malaysia operate within a comprehensive network of government laws and an extensive regulatory system; however, they continue to confront challenges and difficulties concerning non-revenue water, infrastructure renewal, financial rigidity and limited adaptive capacity. The current studies usually assess these difficulties through institutional design and performance indicators. Less attention is given to how governance arrangements are interpreted and enacted by organisational actors. Therefore, this study examines how water utility actors interpret authority, accountability, coordination and operational prudence within Malaysia’s dual federalism (federal-state) governance system, and how institutional and organisational conditions shape cross-case distinction. The study used an interpretive qualitative cross-case design involving four states in Northern Malaysia (Perlis, Kedah, Pulau Pinang and Perak water utilities) and the National Water Services Commission (SPAN). Data and information were collected from 24 semi-structured interviews with senior organisational actors. It is also endorsed by documented records, operational outputs and performance evidence which were analysed through a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic process using the revised OECD Water Governance Framework as a sensitising device. The findings indicate a recurring paradox of control: strong regulatory oversight reinforces procedural discipline, service stability and vertical accountability, while limited authority over raw water, tariffs, major financing decisions and cross-agency coordination restrict local discretion and adaptive problem-solving. Institutional maturity which is conveyed through leadership continuity, financial capacity, technical systems and organisational routines is the meditated conditions whether the same regulatory regime is experienced as navigable or burdensome. The study advances an interpretive explanation of governance effectiveness and identifies practical reforms to align authority, accountability, resources and adaptive capacity for more sustainable water service delivery.
